  • And if you are ever left with a standing town centre and nobody at all to work it, somebody wanders in out of the trees after a while and takes up the work. Only ever down to nought, and never as an income
Carrying it home
  • What a villager is carrying used to be a small coloured square floating by their head from the first swing of the axe. Now you see nothing until they turn for home — and then it is in both arms: logs with the cut ends showing, blocks of stone, ingots of gold or iron, a basket of berries, or moonstone that gives off its own light
  • The axe goes away for the walk. You cannot carry an armful of logs and swing a felling axe at the same time
  • And a miner swings a pickaxe now, rather than the same axe the berry-pickers carry
Dressed for the work
  • You can tell what somebody does by looking at them now. Anyone out in the fields is in a broad straw hat, anyone at the trees is in a woodcutter's check flannel, and anyone up at the stone, gold, iron or moonstone wears a hard hat with a lamp on the front — and once it is dark, that lamp is lit
  • It follows the work and not the villager, so somebody sent from the woods up to the quarry has changed by the time they get there
Things to do
  • Seven more ways for somebody off duty to spend an afternoon, on top of watching the farm, skipping stones, reading under a tree and flying a kite. One will sit down outside the town centre and play a guitar. Another will stand and sing — and the singing spreads: whoever is near enough to hear stops what they are doing and goes off humming it themselves, so a whole corner of the village ends up at it. Someone else will stand about working a yo-yo. And someone will pick a bunch of flowers and go and give them to whoever is nearest
  • Three of them belong to a season and only turn up in it. A snowball is winter — and whoever gets hit packs one and throws it straight back. A running jump into a pile of leaves is autumn, leaves and all. And a puddle the rain left behind is there to be jumped in, as anybody stood too close finds out
  • The whole batch is people doing things to each other rather than beside each other. There are rather more of them out and about, too: with a dozen things to do and half of them seasonal, the old rate meant you could watch a whole afternoon and see two
Patch 21.11
Auto mode
  • Double-tap a villager to put just that one into Auto mode — the panel below says so. From then on, every tap does whatever actually makes sense there: attack an enemy, gather a resource, repair or join a build, garrison a watchtower as its lookout, or board a boat, all without arming an action button first
  • Tap bare ground to finish: Auto mode ends and the villager is let go, so you are left with nothing selected and can get straight on with something else. Before, there was no way out of it except tapping the villager themselves, which nobody found — and a tap on open ground just walked them over there instead. Tapping the villager still drops out of Auto mode as well, and it lets go on its own if they stop being your only selection, or if they die
Build menu
  • Build now opens onto five categories — Military, Food & Wood, Gold & Stone, Knowledge, Village — instead of one long sideways scroll through everything at once. Military leads with whatever actually trains a unit before the walls, towers and upgrades that don't
  • The rare one-villager unlocks (a seasonal crop, the Wildlings' Den, the Hermit's Cottage) still show the moment you open Build, above the categories, so they're never missed
Seasonal realism
  • A puddle now actually means something to walk through, not just a passing decal — ground still wet from a downpour or squall slows anyone crossing it, easing off as the puddle itself dries up
  • Sunflowers turn up here and there once summer's properly in, growing tall out of the ordinary wildflower patches rather than a whole field of them appearing at once
Groups
  • Group 1 is always the Town Centre now, not a spare numbered slot — tap it to select it, tap it twice to bring the camera straight home
Village life
  • The off-duty villagers who come out of the houses — the ones who watch the farm, skip stones, read under a tree or fly a kite — are drawn as the very same people as the villagers working around them: the same build, the same height, the same walk. They had a smaller, plainer figure all of their own before, which is why they never quite looked like they belonged. Only their clothes set them apart now, which was always the idea. They dress for the winter along with everybody else, too, and they have finally put the woodcutting axe down — one of them was flying a kite with it still in his fist
  • They no longer keep to their own doorstep. Somebody off duty will now walk right across the village to call in somewhere else — the bakery, the barracks, the town centre — and they find their way round whatever is in between rather than stopping against it
  • And one errand is no longer the whole afternoon: about half the time they will go on somewhere else before heading home, up to a couple more stops
  • They stop and talk, as well. Somebody on their way past an idle or gathering villager may pull up for a word — both of them stand and face each other for a few seconds, then get on with it. Two off-duty villagers who meet on the path will do the same, and someone will happily walk up to whoever is sat reading under a tree and interrupt them
  • And your own working villagers now do it themselves. Two of them at the same patch of woods will occasionally down tools for a few seconds, have a word, and get straight back to it — they never leave the job you gave them, never lose their order, and never do it while there is fighting in the village
Weather
  • A thunderstorm's rain no longer falls as one ruled sheet of identical streaks — every drop has its own weight, length, angle and speed now, the nearer ones heavier and brighter, and the whole downpour leans and slides as the gust comes and goes
Fixed
  • Moonstone Villagers could be trained and then had nothing they could actually do — gathering, building, and joining a building's crew were every one of them gated on being an ordinary villager, which they are not. The night shift works now: it gathers, it builds, it repairs, and it fights
  • The wandering pilgrims used to walk into the water and shuffle about in the shallows for the rest of their visit. They walk on out of sight instead
  • The moonlit hare and stag could end up standing inside a building, sliding through it or wedged against a wall until their next whim took them. They keep out of the walls now, and if a step would put them in one they think better of it and go somewhere else
  • An ancient ruin also punched a hole straight through the black fog when it appeared — it is placed as one of your own buildings so that repairing it works like any other repair, and that quietly gave it a building's eyesight. It lights nothing now until you have actually found it
  • Birds no longer fly over ground nobody has ever set foot on. A skein crossing the black told you there was something out there to see, which is the one thing unexplored fog is for
  • An ancient ruin used to announce itself the moment it appeared, while it was still sitting out in unexplored country. You had to be told about it rather than find it, which rather defeated the point. Nothing is said now until your own people have actually been out there and uncovered it — and once found, it stays found, without introducing itself again every time somebody wanders back past
  • A saved village from before the ancient ruins landed could fail to continue at all. Loading now fills in anything a save is missing from an earlier version, rather than losing the village over it
Patch 21.10
Things to find
  • Five ruins may now turn up somewhere near your village, rarely, one at a time — an old farmhouse, a blacksmith's, a shrine, a watchtower, and a mine. Each is hidden until you actually explore over it, broken, blackened and overgrown until you send villagers to repair it
  • Restored, each one turns out to have been worth finding: a better field than a fresh farm's, a watchtower that sees twice as far, a richer mine, a straight gift of moonstone, and a blacksmith whose own old trick tempers every soldier's armour a little further, at any age — look for a faint violet gleam on their shoulders
  • None of the five vanish once repaired, either — they keep a little of that broken, overgrown look for good, just less of it
Patch 21.9
A fuller night
  • Fishing after dark now pays off properly — a shoal bites better once it's truly deep night, at the Dock or from the bank
  • A falling star can still be wished on, but catch a few in quick succession during a meteor shower and each one sweetens the last
  • A rare, occasional night now brings something out of the ordinary — the first being a lantern festival, every house lit together and the village out and about, with a small reward for everyone while it lasts
  • Rarer still: a night market may set up at the edge of the village, offering better trades than the Trading Post can. Worth it, if you don't mind that buying more raises the odds of trouble before the cart moves on
New building
  • The Noticeboard now doubles as a logbook — open it to see which of the village's rarer sights you've actually come across this match
Patch 21.8
Put right
  • A creature wandering the village at night could walk up to a building and simply stop there, pinned against it for a few seconds, rather than finding its way round. Fixed for all of them — the dog, the wolf, the hare, the stag, and the fox
  • The fox was meant to dart playfully about the village while it lasted, but never actually moved from the spot it appeared in. It does now
Patch 21.7
Things to find
  • Two more moonlit visitors may pass through the village at night, alongside the wolf — each one worth three taps, moonstone every time. Still rare; that's the whole idea
Patch 21.6
New buildings
  • The Bakery — no gathering, no garrison, just an army that fights a little harder once it's standing
  • The Granary — your stores stop going off overnight
  • The Well and the Shrine — small and cheap, and not everything about them is built yet
  • The Blacksmith — every queue you have finishes a little faster while it stands
  • The Observatory — its lantern lights on its own when there's wild moonstone near your village tonight, even before you've found it
  • The Noticeboard — a true fact about the age you're living through, a new one each day
Patch 21.5
Things to find
  • Two more things worth noticing if you come across them — one in the weather, one in a light seen at the edge of the village at night. As before, no more said than that
  • Repairing the ancient ruin also gives every watchtower you hold a look to match — feathers and ivy, not just the extra reach
Put right
  • A creature that leads you somewhere could, rarely, end up leading nowhere at all — stuck across a stretch of water it had no way round. That's fixed, wherever it might have happened
Patch 21.4
Things to find
  • There are three things out in the world now worth noticing if you see them — a flower, a bird, a fox. Each leads somewhere, and each unlocks something new if you follow it through. Deliberately saying no more than that
  • Once a season, at night, a moonstone-coloured wolf may wander into the village. It doesn't mind being tapped — up to three times, and it's worth its while each time
Put right
  • Moonstone veins light the ground properly now — a real pool punched out of the dark, the same way a brazier's does, rather than a faint halo that was never bright enough to actually find one by
  • A watchtower's garrison — its archers and any villager keeping watch — can be released one at a time by tapping their face, the same as a barracks or range already worked
Patch 21.3
New building
  • The Caretaker's Cottage, in the Iron Age. It keeps your fields reseeded for you — no more hunting down a bare farm and tapping Replenish yourself
The night watch
  • A villager can be posted in a watchtower as a lookout, in a slot of their own alongside its four archers — the tower's panel now shows both counts separately
  • Spot moonstone from up there and they head straight out for it
  • Villagers get a Garrison button in place of Stop, since that's rather more useful to have to hand
Getting resources home
  • The Lumber Camp, Mine, Town Centre and Moonstone Manor each take deliveries at two points now, front and back. Boxed in on one side, a carrier finds the other instead of waiting on a wall that has no door
Put right
  • The cat known as Dog no longer walks on water
  • A villager worked a second night running with no rest used to drop dead without warning. There is a real stretch of time now where it shows on them and sending them home in time saves them
  • The Ashkin's villagers no longer sense — or wander into your town to mine — your Moonstone Manor's own vein
  • The fix that stopped the elder and the pilgrims leaning on a house forever only caught it once they were nearly there. A target properly walled in behind several buildings now gives up too, rather than pacing the outside of it for the rest of the match
Patch 21.2
Clearing ground
  • Villagers and moonstone villagers have a Remove button. Tap it, then tap a tree or a berry bush and it is gone on the spot — useful when the plot you want to build on has something standing in it
  • Nothing is carried home for it. It is not a harvest, it is getting the thing out of the way
  • It stays switched on so you can clear several in a row. It will not take a farm's crop, a shoal, stone, gold or moonstone, nor a tree your lumber camp was built to work
The town centre
  • It has a chimney at last — the tallest building in the village had a cold hearth while every cottage around it smoked. It draws harder while somebody is being trained inside
  • What has just been carried in is stacked by the door until it is put away
  • Its windows keep the hours now instead of blazing away at noon, and there is a lantern lit by the door after dark
  • The year leaves something on the step — blooms in spring, a leaning sheaf in autumn, snow shovelled aside in winter
  • A few chickens peck about in front of it by day, and go to roost after dark
Overhead
  • Some clear nights the sky will not keep still — one streak after another, for a minute or two, and then it settles
  • On a full moon, and only then, someone walks through by moonlight with the ground going pale where they pass. Notice them and they leave something behind
Out in the country
  • Rabbits have burrows. They graze within sight of one and bolt down it when anyone comes near, and put their heads out again a while later
  • Where there has been fighting, crows come by afterwards and wheel over the place for a time
  • Locusts can come down on a night's fields and strip a share of what is standing. A bad night, not a ruined harvest
  • Moonstone is twice as common at night. It was never as scarce as it looked — it is only ever out between dusk and dawn, and nobody is awake to notice
Put right
  • Peaceful means peaceful. The Ashkin will not march on you at all — not after twenty-five minutes, not ever — unless you go for them first. Defending your own ground does not count; going to their side of the valley does, and you will be told the day it happens
  • The Manor's own vein comes back. Mined flat, it had been gone for the rest of the match; it now fills again over two or three nights
  • Moonstone stops being minable at dawn, as it always should have — anyone still working a vein when the sun came up carried on all day
  • Moonstone glows harder after dark, and comes up earlier in the evening, so a vein is easier to come across — brighter again since, and there is a third more of it in your own veins each night. The Ashkin's are as they were
  • The elder and the pilgrims no longer lean on the side of a house for ever when the way round is blocked
  • The seasonal crop can no longer grow inside a tree, where it could not be picked
  • Butterflies keep off the trunks
  • Moonstone no longer comes up under a tree. Near enough half of every night's veins were sharing their ground with one, and a third of them were hidden behind it entirely — which was rather more to blame for veins being hard to find than the dark was. Veins now look for open ground, and on a night when there is none to be had they push the tree aside
  • Musicians can be told to follow your soldiers, which is rather the point of them — the order was offered and then refused
People and time
  • The days and nights are a fifth longer. More time in each, fewer of them in a match
  • The folk who step outside their houses look like the rest of the village now — hair, beards, scarves, hats, and no two quite the same height
  • The mark villagers were muttering that looked like a letter L has gone. Their chatter is meant to be wordless
  • One night event is away while it is rethought — the one that ringed a stray soldier with figures
Patch 21.1
  • Your village keeps itself now. It saves at every dawn, and the ☰ menu has a Save of its own for putting it down mid-afternoon
  • Continue on the start menu picks it back up — the same morning, the same people, the same ground you had walked
  • There is one village at a time. Starting a new game says so before it takes the old one
  • The start screen is a menu: new game, continue, how to play, settings, and these notes
  • Choosing a difficulty deals the match and shows you how to play before it starts — nothing moves until you say Begin
  • Settings can delete a saved village. There will be more in there before long
  • The island deals are away for the moment while the boats are finished
And out of the window
  • Flocks lean with the wind now — the same wind the chimney smoke and the grass have always leaned with
  • When the weather really gets up, the sky empties. Birds make for the nearest edge, the gulls stop coming, and the ridges clear until it eases
  • Twice a year a long skein crosses the whole map — away south as the leaves turn, back again in spring
  • The day has a round to it. Small things keep to the half-light at either end, deer come out into the open in the afternoon, and the big ones move at night
  • Something dry and brittle blows through on a windy summer or autumn afternoon
  • Frogs sit at the water's edge and hop, mostly nowhere. Walk up to one and it is gone
  • Every so often somebody's sheep gets out and ambles across your valley
  • The rain in a downpour falls a little slower, so it reads as rain rather than static
Patch 20.9
  • Moonstone is worth going out for now — the veins are richer, and they glow through ground you have already explored
  • Spend enough of it and you can raise something new in the Bronze Age. By day it works crystal; after dark it is a different building entirely
  • It comes with a vein of its own that never quite runs dry
  • There are people who keep the opposite hours to your village. They light the ground they walk on
  • They throw moonstone at anything that comes for your town, and whatever it hits does not shrug it off
  • Daylight does not suit them. You can work them through it, but not for ever
  • Give them somewhere of their own to live and there will be more of them — and little ones out after dark
  • Villagers can finally be put in a numbered group, with a tool of their own on the button
  • A night in their own bed mends anyone a little — whichever hours they keep
  • Longer messages now stay up long enough to actually be read
  • Fewer folk drifting out of doors, and the whales move on after a day or two
  • Moonstone comes up in three separate places around your village, and not every night — a night it does is worth staying up for
  • Fixed: dogs and children wandering out into the water
  • Fixed: the bottom row of buttons sitting too close to the edge on an iPad
  • Buildings can be worked through with crystal, once you have somewhere to work it — faster at whatever they do, and a light of their own after dark
  • Every kind of building takes the crystal differently: a seam through a field, a spine up a watchtower, a crown on the round roofs, spikes along a barracks
  • After dark a worked building is traced by the faintest blue line, and the crystal breathes very slowly — you will only catch it if you stop and watch one
  • The Ashkin get all of this too, if they ever get round to it. Moonstone is an indulgence, not their first thought
Patch 20.8
  • Something worth finding grows out in the deep country once a season. Bring it home and plant it
  • A new farm that does more than feed you
  • More moonstone after dark, and something that will show you the way
  • A full moon is worth more than a new one
  • Fireflies on warm nights, and two new sights in the sky
  • The rare sights are tuned to turn up about one match in five — so no single game shows you everything, and there is always something you have not seen yet
Patch 20.7
  • Braziers can be rebuilt once an age, each one on its own
  • Every rebuild throws its light further and stands up to more
  • And looks the part
Patch 20.6
  • The village settles in for the night gradually, house by house
  • Birds on your roofs, wind through the grass and smoke, and the odd shooting star
  • Buildings show their age. So do the people living in them
  • An almanac line at the bottom of the screen tells you about today
Patch 20.5
  • Twenty animals that only live well outside the town — five for each season
  • Squirrels, ducks, dragonflies, and a fox that never quite catches anything
  • Villagers take days off. Tap one to see who they are
  • Children, dogs, weather underfoot, and footprints in fresh snow
  • More happens at night
  • The Ashkin can cross to your island properly and attack together
